root_cause: The AKS subnet's UDR sends all egress (0.0.0.0/0) to the Azure Firewall, but the firewall policy's application rule collections were written without the AzureKubernetesService FQDN tag and without explicit allow rules for mcr.microsoft.com and *.data.mcr.microsoft.com. The denied application-rule log entries for mcr.microsoft.com and data.mcr.microsoft.com are what break node image pulls, so nodes flip NotReady intermittently; the allowed entries for login.microsoftonline.com and blob storage are why other outbound traffic still works.
evidence: az-aks-show.json: outboundType is userDefinedRouting, so AKS egress follows the route table instead of the managed load balancer
az-network-route-table-show.json: route DefaultRouteToFirewall sends 0.0.0.0/0 to the firewall appliance at 10.20.1.4

az-network-firewall-policy-rule-collection.json: application rule collections allow login.microsoftonline.com, management.azure.com, and *.blob.core.windows.net but contain no AzureKubernetesService FQDN tag and no mcr.microsoft.com FQDNs
azfw-application-rule-log.kql.csv: Denied entries (no rule matched) for mcr.microsoft.com and data.mcr.microsoft.com while login.microsoftonline.com and blob endpoints are Allowed
kubectl-describe-pod.txt: ImagePull timeout dialing mcr.microsoft.com:443 for the istio sidecar while the ACR image pulled successfully over its private endpoint
fix: Add an application rule collection to the firewall policy that allows the AzureKubernetesService FQDN tag (or explicit allow rules for mcr.microsoft.com and *.data.mcr.microsoft.com) over HTTPS for the AKS subnet sources, so node image pulls from MCR succeed again.
